text:
ana: Heads-up — after the RBAC shadow rollout this morning (~09:12 UTC) we're seeing intermittent TLS handshakes failing at EU edge proxies. Logs show KMS unwrap denies on a subset of requests. Anyone already looking?

mike: saw a spike in handshake errors ~09:18, correlated to proxy-eu-3 pool. Quick logs: 

```
proxy_eu3 09:18:12 ERR handshake failed keystore.unwrap: kms:AccessDenied principal=service-account:edge-proxy-eu region=eu-west-1
sni=\"app.customer.internal\" conn_id=0x7f4a3c
```

ana: (sorry, meant to ping) ana: I think the RBAC shadow rollout touched the keystore role mapping PR. It was shadow-only, but there was a configpublish race that could flip the enforcement flag on a small % of hosts.
devon: confirming — we saw a kubeconfig rollout job that updated the DaemonSet with new env var RBAC_ENFORCE=true on 3 pods by accident. Those pods are in the eu proxy pool.

raj: if the pods started enforcing, they'd hit KMS deny for wrapped keys if role mapping wasn't provisioned. That matches. Are the KMS denies coming from the edge pod principal or the proxy service principal?
mike: logs show principal=proxy-service-role (not the new role mapping). So looks like role mapping mismatch — the proxies are asserting a principal that KMS policy doesn't allow to decrypt.

sec-bot: Alert: KMS Unwrap Deny count elevated for project=redwood-edge/eu region=eu-west-1. New alarms triggered: kms.unwrap.denies > 50/min. Linked audit logs: https://console.audit/kms/unwrap?time=09:10-09:30

ana: Immediate mitigation options: 1) revert the env var change to set RBAC_ENFORCE=false on eu proxies, 2) add a temporary allow in KMS policy for the proxy-service-role (wide blast, risky), 3) route traffic away from affected proxy-eu-3 to eu-legacy pool via routing-policy. Thoughts?
devon: prefer revert to shadow mode — smallest blast radius and preserves KMS policy posture. Can oncall revert DS?
oncall: I'm on it. Reverting the DS now, will cordon and restart 3 pods in proxy-eu-3. ETA ~5m.

mike: also recommend enabling detailed audit logs for the rotator service and adding correlation id to keystore unwrap calls: add header X-Keystore-Request-ID to link TLS handshake -> KMS audit entry. That helps postmortem.

raj: agree. Long term we should: 1) enforce preflight that prevents RBAC_ENFORCE=true rolling into any pool without having role bindings present, 2) add canary gating to the configpublish job, 3) add KMS deny sampling alerts that include principal and pod metadata.

ana: quick triage notes for incident ticket: root cause = configpublish race enabling RBAC enforcement on subset of EU proxies without corresponding keystore role bindings in KMS. Impact = intermittent handshake failures, customer-facing connection errors for EU region 09:12-09:24 UTC.

sec-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0427-12. Link: https://incidents/redwood/INC-2026-0427-12

mike: small snippet to add to postmortem for logs correlation: 

```
# correlate by X-Keystore-Request-ID
grep \"keystore.unwrap\" /var/log/proxy/*.log | jq -R 'split(\" \") | {ts:.[0], msg:.[1], principal:.[5], sni:.[9]}'
```

devon: oncall said revert finished — can confirm?
oncall: revert done at 09:22 UTC. Pod restarts completed, rolling checks show unwrap denies dropping to baseline. Last deny seen 09:23:41.

raj: moving to postmortem actions: - block configpublish job from setting RBAC_ENFORCE=true unless role-bindings exist (OWNER: devops) - add KMS policy test in CI to simulate unwrap with proxy principal (OWNER: infra) - add circuit-breaker routing to avoid single pool blast (OWNER: networking)

ana: assigning draft postmortem, I'll take write-up. Please add any logs or KMS audit links you used.
mike: adding the relevant KMS audit links and the proxy logs to the ticket now.

sec-bot: Reminder: add CVE tracking checklist if any customer certs were rotated or reissued.

ana: noted — no cert reissue performed. We only toggled enforcement. No private key exposure observed.

devon: follow-up: propose we implement cached local key fallback for a short TTL so keystore unwrap failures don't immediately break handshakes during role/provisioning windows. Will draft design.

raj: good idea — ensure TTL respects key rotation window. Keep in mind HSM/KMS compliance constraints.

ana: thanks everyone. Closing slack triage thread; moving discussion to postmortem doc.

oncall: closing loop — alerts suppressed and incident marked mitigated. :white_check_mark:
